skill.name: steel-browser
skill.description: Run Steel cloud browser sessions for web navigation, scraping, screenshots, PDFs, form flows, and session-based automation.
skill.summary: Automate remote browser workflows with Steel cloud sessions and web extraction tools.
skill.author: steel-dev

security_audit.summary: Most static hits are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, placeholder URLs, documented API-key setup, or example artifact paths. The confirmed concerns are semantic: the skill intentionally supports anti-bot and CAPTCHA workflows, defaults to Steel cloud routing for many web tasks, and can inject credentials into remote sessions.

remediation.issue: Anti-bot and CAPTCHA automation is presented as a normal workflow.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user authorization, document site-policy constraints, and keep CAPTCHA, proxy, and stealth features off by default.

remediation.issue: Cloud browser use can happen even when the user does not ask for Steel.
remediation.suggestion: Add consent language before sending private URLs, page content, credentials, screenshots, PDFs, or form data to Steel cloud.

remediation.issue: Credential injection and API key handling are spread across multiple references.
remediation.suggestion: Centralize secret-handling rules, never echo keys, and require user-provided credential namespaces for authenticated sessions.

remediation.issue: Static analysis flags many documentation examples as executable shell risks.
remediation.suggestion: Reduce scanner noise by replacing shell command substitution examples with fixed placeholder session names where possible.

semantic_findings.title: Anti-Bot Evasion and CAPTCHA Bypass
semantic_findings.description: The skill tells agents to use Steel for anti-bot-sensitive automation and documents stealth, proxy, CAPTCHA status, and CAPTCHA solve workflows.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The files explicitly say to trigger for anti-bot-sensitive automation and provide stealth, proxy, and CAPTCHA solving commands. Legitimate testing is possible, but the bypass capability is clear.

semantic_findings.title: Default Cloud Browser Routing Without Explicit User Request
semantic_findings.description: The skill says to trigger even when the user does not mention Steel and defaults to cloud mode, which can send URLs, page content, and interactions to Steel cloud.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The trigger and mode instructions clearly prefer cloud Steel for remote web tasks. The files include some exclusions for localhost and private networks, so the risk is data exposure rather than clear malice.

semantic_findings.title: Credential Injection Into Remote Browser Sessions
semantic_findings.description: The references describe stored credentials, credential namespaces, and credential injection into Steel sessions, which can expose account access in remote browser contexts.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Credential injection is explicitly documented, and remote browser sessions are sensitive. The docs also mention redaction and key guardrails, so the concern is controlled but real.

content.value_statement: Web tasks often fail when pages need JavaScript, sessions, or visual verification. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through Steel browser sessions and extraction commands.
actual_capabilities: Starts, reuses, inspects, and stops named Steel browser sessions.
Scrapes web pages into markdown or HTML through Steel API tools.
Captures webpage screenshots and PDFs for visual review.
Runs browser interactions such as open, click, fill, wait, snapshot, and get text.
Guides migration from agent-browser commands to Steel browser commands.
Provides troubleshooting steps for auth, endpoint, session, and CAPTCHA issues.
limitations: Requires Steel CLI access and Steel authentication before cloud sessions work.
Cloud sessions cannot reach localhost or private network targets unless exposed to Steel.
Automation must follow site terms, user authorization, and applicable law.
CAPTCHA, proxy, and stealth workflows may require paid Steel features and explicit consent.

use_cases.title: Collect Dynamic Web Content
use_cases.description: Extract content from JavaScript-heavy pages when a simple fetch does not show the needed data.

use_cases.title: Verify Web Workflows
use_cases.description: Drive a remote browser through clicks, forms, waits, and snapshots to confirm an online flow.

use_cases.title: Create Page Artifacts
use_cases.description: Capture screenshots or PDFs of public web pages for reports, reviews, or records.

prompt_templates.title: Scrape a Page
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner extraction from one public URL.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Steel Browser to scrape <url>. Return the main content, headings, and any missing or blocked sections.

prompt_templates.title: Capture Visual Artifacts
prompt_templates.scenario: Create evidence from a rendered web page.
prompt_templates.prompt: Open <url> in a Steel session. Capture a screenshot and PDF, then summarize what each artifact shows.

prompt_templates.title: Complete a Form Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Start a named Steel session for <url>. Inspect the page, fill the requested fields, submit, and verify the result.

prompt_templates.title: Debug a Blocked Session
prompt_templates.prompt: Diagnose why my Steel Browser task against <url> is blocked. Check auth, mode, session reuse, CAPTCHA status, and proxy settings.

output_examples.input: Extract public pricing details from a product page.
output_examples.output: Returns a concise pricing summary, lists plan names and limits, and notes content that required browser rendering.

output_examples.input: Capture a screenshot and PDF of a report page.
output_examples.output: Creates visual artifacts, confirms the page title, and reports any dynamic sections that may need another capture.

output_examples.input: Recover an authorized workflow after a CAPTCHA appears.
output_examples.output: Reports session state, CAPTCHA status, and permission-aware next steps for manual solving or proxy configuration.

best_practices: Ask for permission before sending private URLs, credentials, or page data to a cloud browser.
Use one named session per workflow and stop sessions when work is complete.
Prefer scrape, screenshot, or PDF commands before using step-by-step browser control.
anti_patterns: Do not use cloud sessions for localhost or private network targets without explicit exposure.
Do not run CAPTCHA, proxy, or stealth workflows without clear user authorization.
Do not print API keys, connect URLs with secrets, cookies, or credential values.

faq.question: What does this skill automate?
faq.answer: It guides Steel CLI browser sessions, scraping, screenshots, PDFs, and authorized page interactions.

faq.question: Does it need a Steel account?
faq.answer: Yes. Cloud browser use requires Steel authentication through login or an API key.

faq.question: Can it access localhost apps?
faq.answer: Not through default cloud sessions. Use local or self-hosted Steel only when the user requests that mode.

faq.question: Can it solve CAPTCHAs?
faq.answer: The references describe CAPTCHA status and solve commands. Use them only with user authorization and site permission.

faq.question: Can it migrate agent-browser commands?
faq.answer: Yes. It maps agent-browser command prefixes to steel browser commands and adds lifecycle handling.

faq.question: What data may leave the local machine?
faq.answer: Target URLs, page content, screenshots, PDFs, session metadata, and submitted form data may pass through Steel cloud.
